Human performs the stage. The system makes no meaningful task-specific contribution to the applicable stage.
Limited assistance. The system performs a narrow fragment or supplies cues; the human performs the principal work.
Substantial partial performance. The system performs substantial components, but a human materially supplies, integrates, corrects, or completes the stage.
Complete stage with routine human gate. The system produces a stage-complete output for supported cases, but routine human validation, approval, release, or technical supervision remains.
Complete stage without routine human gate. The system completes and releases or executes the stage without routine substantive human review, approval, correction, or execution.
Not applicable. The AIDA stage is genuinely absent from the frozen task scope.
Insufficient evidence. The stage applies, but the available evidence cannot support a rating.
The stated applicability scope ordinarily cannot proceed without documented human authority at this stage.
Human authority is required only when a named, non-hypothetical condition is present.
The stage applies, but the protocol search found no documented pre-effect human-authority requirement within the stated scope.
The stage is absent from the frozen task scope and must match capability and product-design applicability.
The stage applies, but the rule, jurisdiction, signatory, timing, or applicability cannot be determined reliably.
Legal or professional authority. Law, regulation, licensing, or professional rules reserve authorization to a human.
A licensed physician must sign the report.
Organizational governance. Employer, buyer, contract, procurement rule, separation of duties, or vendor policy requires approval.
Company requires review before AI-generated code is deployed.
Liability or safety. Human review is retained because potential harm is severe, irreversible, or requires accountable responsibility.
Clinician approves treatment; executive authorizes a large payment.
Rights, privacy, or security. Review protects due process, fairness, confidentiality, access control, or cybersecurity.
Human reviews a benefits denial or release of medical records.
Trust or ethical legitimacy. Customers or society expect a human to remain responsible for sensitive judgment or communication.
Workforce or economics. Labor agreements, skill preservation, staffing considerations, or cost calculations retain human involvement.
Union agreement preserves final employee control.
Other or unknown. Evidence establishes a requirement, but its reason does not fit another category or cannot be determined.
Documentation requires approval without explaining why.
The product-supported case and capability evidence are materially comparable in endpoint, inputs, operating conditions, and difficulty.
The records address the same canonical task and outcome, but one side covers a materially narrower, easier, or otherwise unmatched case.
The records address materially different endpoints or only an adjacent fragment; the numeric gap must not be interpreted.
